levels.title: 2024 songs per genre
levels.task: Stellar Sound wants a quick snapshot of 2024: how many chart songs landed in each genre. Sort so genres with the most songs appear first; if two genres tie, list them A–Z by genre name.
levels.initialCode: -- SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS song_count FROM top_songs WHERE release_date LIKE '2024-%' GROUP BY genre ORDER BY ...
levels.solution:
SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS song_count
FROM top_songs
WHERE release_date LIKE '2024-%'
GROUP BY genre
ORDER BY song_count DESC, genre;
levels.hintMessage: Try WHERE release_date LIKE '2024-%' to lock the year, then GROUP BY genre so each count is per genre.
levels.successMessage: Nice! WHERE picks the rows first, then GROUP BY organizes them by genre.

levels.title: Pop hits over a billion
levels.task: Marketing is making a poster of pop songs with over 1 billion streams. Return each song’s name, artist, and stream count, with the biggest hits at the top.
levels.solution:
SELECT track_name, artist, spotify_streams
FROM top_songs
WHERE genre = 'Pop' AND spotify_streams >= 1000000000
ORDER BY spotify_streams DESC;
levels.hintMessage: Put both tests in one WHERE … AND …. For “at least” a billion, spotify_streams >= 1000000000 does the job.
levels.successMessage: Great! AND keeps only rows that pass BOTH tests.

levels.title: Chart-wide stats in one row
levels.task: Your boss wants a single summary row for the whole chart: total number of songs, sum of all streams, average streams per song, and the longest track by duration (in milliseconds). No filtering—just one row of four numbers.
levels.initialCode: -- SELECT COUNT(*) AS song_count, SUM(...) AS total_streams, AVG(...) AS avg_streams, MAX(...) AS longest_song FROM top_songs;
levels.solution:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS song_count,
  SUM(spotify_streams) AS total_streams,
  AVG(spotify_streams) AS avg_streams,
  MAX(duration_ms) AS longest_song
FROM top_songs;
levels.hintMessage: COUNT(*) and SUM(spotify_streams) are two of the calculations. Skip GROUP BY for this one since we are looking at the whole chart.
levels.successMessage: Perfect! One row, four useful numbers—great for a status email.

levels.title: Pop artists: songs and total streams
levels.task: A&R wants a Pop-only leaderboard: one row per artist showing how many songs they have on the chart and their combined streams. Order by combined streams highest first then by artist name alphabetically.
levels.initialCode: -- SELECT artist, COUNT(*) AS song_count, SUM(spotify_streams) AS total_streams FROM top_songs WHERE genre = 'Pop' GROUP BY artist ORDER BY ...
levels.solution:
SELECT artist, COUNT(*) AS song_count, SUM(spotify_streams) AS total_streams
FROM top_songs
WHERE genre = 'Pop'
GROUP BY artist
ORDER BY total_streams DESC, artist;
levels.hintMessage: WHERE genre = 'Pop' first, then GROUP BY artist. COUNT(*) and SUM(spotify_streams) give songs vs. combined streams per artist.
levels.successMessage: Strong! You filtered, grouped, and stacked two aggregates in one query.

levels.title: Artists on the 2023–2024 chart
levels.task: Stellar Sound is prepping a two-year recap (releases from the start of 2023 through the end of 2024). For each artist, show how many qualifying songs they have and their average streams on those songs. Sort it by artists with the most songs first, then alphabetically by artist name.
levels.initialCode: -- WHERE release_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2024-12-31' GROUP BY artist
levels.solution:
SELECT artist, COUNT(*) AS song_count, AVG(spotify_streams) AS avg_streams
FROM top_songs
WHERE release_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2024-12-31'
GROUP BY artist
ORDER BY song_count DESC, artist;
levels.hintMessage: WHERE release_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2024-12-31' picks the window (inclusive). You will use COUNT() and AVG() for this query.
levels.successMessage: Great work! You combined a date range filter with two aggregates and a group—that's real reporting SQL.
